title: Documentary Suzane von Richthofen: O que o Tempo Não Apaga premieres on November 11 on Netflix
summary: 24 years after the crime, the production features never-before-seen interviews with Suzane, archive footage and statements from people connected to the case
body_markdown:
São Paulo, November 9, 2026 – The documentary


Suzane von Richthofen: O que o Tempo Não Apaga


premieres this Wednesday (11) on Netflix. The production, whose trailer was released today, features never-before-seen interviews with Suzane, convicted of the deaths of her parents, Manfred and Marísia, in São Paulo, in 2002. More than 20 years after the crime, and more than 10 years after her last interview, the documentary investigates who Suzane became after serving part of her sentence and confronts her with what was investigated and established. Archive footage and interviews with experts and people connected to the case round out the narrative.


“More than two decades after the crime, the documentary allows us to discuss subjects that are very dear to our society, such as the media and its impact on this and other similar cases, resocialization, and a bit of the reality of the penal system in Brazil,” says Lygia M. Barbosa, who directs the documentary alongside Paulo Gambale Maká.


Produced by Kromaki, in co-production with Grama Filmes, the documentary has Rodrigo Letier as producer. Executive production is by Roberta Oliveira and Fernanda Abreu. The screenplay is written by Rafael Spínola, Thaís Falcão, Raphael Scire, Jordana Berg, EDT. and Victor Miaciro.


Suzane von Richthofen: O que o Tempo Não Apaga


premieres on November 11, only on Netflix.

About Kromaki


Creator of hits such as


Os Quatro da Candelária


(Netflix),


Isabella: O Caso Nardoni


(Netflix) and


Romário - O Cara


(HBO Max), Kromaki is a production company driven by the desire to explore formats, tones, genres and visions to tell impactful stories on screen. Because we believe series and films should move and surprise, entertain and make people think. Preferably all at once.


About Grama Filmes


São Paulo-based production company with more than 20 years in the audiovisual industry. Grama Filmes has produced advertising, series and documentary features for channels such as NatGeo, Netflix, KBS, HBO, Futura, TV Cultura and NGOs such as WWF. Since 2017 it has co-produced with Europe, South Korea, Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and Taiwan.
